title: Report templates
summary: Choose the laboratory's report layout, preview it on synthetic data, and approve or reject a drafted layout.

sections.title: How layouts work
paragraphs: The laboratory has one active report layout. It decides how a released report's PDF is arranged: where the header, the patient, order and specimen details, and the results appear. The content is the same in every layout: patient, order, specimen, every result with its units and limits, the engine's comparison wording, notes, medications as supplied, tests not reported, specimen validity and the person who prepared the release.

A change of layout is a draft until a quality manager approves it. An administrator saves a ready-made layout as a draft; a quality manager previews it and approves it, or rejects it with a reason. Only one draft can wait at a time.

Every candidate records the layout in force when it is prepared, and its PDF is stored once. Approving another layout never changes a released report, its PDF or a candidate already prepared. The layout used is shown on each released revision under Layout.

In every layout except Classic, Meets cutoff is shown as a red label and Does not meet cutoff as a green label; Not classifiable is grey. The engine sends both the wording and its code; the layout only chooses the colour and never interprets a result.

sections.title: Previews
paragraphs: Preview opens the layout as a PDF in a report window. It is filled with one built-in synthetic report (TEST LAB, patient Test, Patient) and never with laboratory data. Every page is marked PREVIEW – NOT A REPORT. A preview is not stored and is not a report.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Preview the draft before deciding, and check that the report number, revision, completeness, report type, patient identity and every result with its limits remain easy to find. After approval, prepare a candidate for a synthetic or routine specimen and check its PDF before release.
Give a rejection reason that the administrator can act on, such as which part of the layout is hard to read.

pages.title: Report templates
pages.purpose: See which report layout is active, compare the ready-made layouts with a preview, save a layout as a draft and approve or reject the draft.
pages.access: Administrators (manage configuration) and quality managers (manage quality) open the page and preview layouts. Only manage configuration saves a draft; only manage quality approves or rejects one. The person who drafted a layout approves it only when the laboratory's separation-of-duties policy allows configuration self-approval, and then must confirm it.

fields.name: Status (page header)
fields.meaning: The layout reports use now and any draft waiting for approval.
fields.values: Active: <layout>, or Active: <layout>, <layout> waiting for approval.
fields.rules: Read-only; changes when a draft is saved, approved or rejected.

fields.name: Active layout: Layout / Version
fields.meaning: The layout every candidate prepared from now on uses.
fields.values: Standard, Compact, Results first or Classic. Version N for an approved version; Built-in default, never approved while the laboratory has approved none (the Classic layout).

fields.name: Active layout: Approved by / Approved
fields.meaning: Who approved the active version and when.
fields.values: The approver's display name and the time in the laboratory's time zone.
fields.rules: Shown only for an approved version.

fields.name: Waiting for approval: Layout / Version / Drafted by / Drafted
fields.meaning: The draft that a quality manager must decide.
fields.values: Layout name, version number, the administrator's display name and the draft time.
fields.rules: The section is shown only while a draft exists. A draft affects no report.

fields.name: Layouts (cards)
fields.meaning: The ready-made layouts: a thumbnail of the first page of its preview, its name and a short description.
fields.values: Standard: a header band with the laboratory and the report number, Patient, Order and Specimen in three cards, a results table and the preparation details. Compact: a dense report meant for one page, with a patient strip at the top and a results table. Results first: the results at the top as large cards, with the order and specimen details after them. Classic: the original single-column layout.
fields.rules: A card is marked Active or Waiting for approval when it is the active layout or the draft. Long reports can still run to more pages in any layout.

fields.name: History
fields.meaning: Every drafted layout version, newest first.
fields.values: Version, Layout, Status (Waiting for approval, Active, Superseded, Rejected), Drafted (who and when), Approved or rejected (who and when, or Not yet) and Rejection reason.
fields.rules: Read-only. Versions are never deleted. An approval supersedes the previous active version.

fields.name: Reason (Reject dialog)
fields.rules: Required. Kept with the version and in the audit trail.

actions.name: Preview
actions.does: Opens the layout as a PDF on built-in synthetic data in a report window, marked PREVIEW – NOT A REPORT on every page.
actions.availableWhen: Always on this page: on the active layout, the draft and every card.
actions.result: Nothing is stored or audited as a report; no laboratory data is used. If the window does not open, the refusal is shown at the top of the page.

actions.name: Save as draft
actions.does: After confirmation, records the layout as a draft waiting for approval.
actions.availableWhen: Manage configuration, no draft waiting, and the card is not the active layout.
actions.result: The draft appears under Waiting for approval and in History. Reports keep using the active layout. Recorded in the audit trail as report.draft_layout.

actions.name: Approve (Approve layout)
actions.does: After confirmation, makes the draft the active layout and supersedes the previous active version.
actions.availableWhen: Manage quality, while a draft waits. The draft's author must be allowed configuration self-approval by the laboratory's separation-of-duties policy and confirm it; otherwise a second person must approve.
actions.result: Candidates prepared from now on use the layout. Released reports, their PDFs and candidates already prepared are unchanged. Recorded as report.approve_layout, marked as a self-approval when the author approved.

actions.name: Reject (Reject layout)
actions.does: Rejects the draft with a reason.
actions.availableWhen: Manage quality, while a draft waits.
actions.result: The active layout stays in use; the draft is kept in History as Rejected with the reason. Recorded as report.reject_layout. A new draft can then be saved.

restrictions: Only the ready-made layouts can be chosen; their arrangement, colours and wording cannot be edited here.
There is one active layout for the whole laboratory; it cannot differ by client or test.
Approving a layout never re-renders or redates an issued report. A report already prepared as a candidate keeps the layout it recorded; prepare a new candidate to use the new layout before release.
A preview uses fixed synthetic data and is not evidence that the layout suits every report the laboratory issues.
workflow: Open Reports › Report templates and preview the layouts.
As an administrator, choose Save as draft on the layout to propose.
As a quality manager, open the page, Preview the draft under Waiting for approval, then Approve or Reject with a reason.
After approval, prepare a candidate and check the PDF. On a released revision, the Layout fact names the layout it was printed with.

troubleshooting.problem: Save as draft is not shown.
troubleshooting.recovery: A draft is already waiting, the card is the active layout, or you lack manage configuration. Ask a quality manager to decide the waiting draft.

troubleshooting.problem: Approve is refused because a second person is required.
troubleshooting.recovery: You drafted this layout and the laboratory's separation-of-duties policy does not allow configuration self-approval. Ask another quality manager to approve it.

troubleshooting.problem: The record changed since it was shown.
troubleshooting.recovery: Someone decided or replaced the draft meanwhile. Reload the page and review the current draft before acting.

troubleshooting.problem: A new report still uses the previous layout.
troubleshooting.recovery: Its candidate was prepared before the approval. Prepare a new candidate; the released revision's Layout fact shows the layout used.
